evidence: app/package.json:5 — @gracile/gracile pinned exactly to 0.11.0, the current stable release (npm latest, ~6 months old)
app/src/routes/(home).js:1 — defineRoute from @gracile/gracile/route used in all 8 route files; core, documented, but recently-stable in central places
app/src/document.js:1 — html from @gracile/gracile/server-html, framework's documented document API
app/vite.config.js:5 — gracile plugin with output: 'server', documented server mode
app/src/routes/(home).client.js — plain vanilla DOM scripting instead of Gracile's experimental CSR add-on
reach.rationale: No experimental flags, add-ons, or prereleases at all — but every central feature (routing, SSR, server adapter) rests on a framework whose latest stable is only ~6 months old and which its own docs label alpha-state, i.e. recently-stable APIs in central places.

evidence: app/server.js:4-20 — entire framework/server integration isolated to one small file, matching the documented Express adapter pattern verbatim
app/vite.config.js:1-8 — framework config is 6 lines, single place to change
app/src/lib/api.js:1-60 — all data fetching centralized in one module, framework-agnostic
app/src/routes/(home).js:1, app/src/routes/pokemon/[name].js:1 — defineRoute spread across 8 route files (inherent to file-based routing)
containment.rationale: Nothing experimental is used, so there is little to contain; the framework-coupled glue lives in server.js and vite.config.js, and the data layer is isolated — though the defineRoute/document pattern necessarily appears in every route file.

evidence: app/vite.config.js:5 — output: 'server' is the only mode that satisfies the spec's request-time data requirement over HTTP
app/server.js:11 — getClientBuildPath + nodeAdapter is the documented stable Express path, not a custom or exotic adapter
app/src/routes/(home).client.js:1-78 — vanilla DOM/History/DOMParser instead of the experimental CSR add-on: same functionality with zero experimental surface
app/package.json:5 — exact version pin on a pre-1.0 framework is deliberate churn-risk management
justification.rationale: Each use of the young framework is the documented, conservative option a stable API couldn't beat, and the riskiest framework feature (CSR add-on, experimental per the docs) is avoided in favor of plain browser APIs.

findings.issue: The whole app rests on Gracile 0.11.0, a pre-1.0 framework whose own docs say it is in an 'alpha state'; breaking changes across 0.x releases are expected for a codebase owned for years.
findings.suggestion: Keep the exact version pin, track 0.x release notes, and keep the framework surface thin (server.js + vite.config.js) so migrations are localized; the spec mandates the framework, so this is a monitored risk rather than a defect.

findings.issue: trailingSlash: 'ignore' could not be confirmed in the current Gracile docs; silently-accepted plugin options are a trap if it ever does nothing or changes meaning.
findings.suggestion: Verify against the plugin reference in the Gracile docs (or its TypeScript types); drop it if it has no effect on this app's URLs.

findings.issue: res.locals.requestId = crypto.randomUUID() is copied from the docs' adapter example but no route ever reads locals.requestId — dead boilerplate coupled to a young framework convention.
findings.suggestion: Delete the middleware (or actually surface the request ID) rather than shipping doc-sample boilerplate verbatim.

summary: The app uses zero experimental, preview, or canary APIs: it sticks to Gracile 0.11.0's documented core (defineRoute, server-html, the Express adapter), pins the exact version, and deliberately skips the framework's one explicitly experimental feature (the CSR add-on) in favor of plain vanilla client scripts. The only structural risk is that the mandated framework itself is a pre-1.0, alpha-labeled release roughly six months old, which the app mitigates by keeping framework glue confined to server.js, vite.config.js and the document template.

experimentalApis.api: Gracile core APIs (defineRoute, server-html, node adapter, plugin output: 'server')
experimentalApis.source: npm registry (@gracile/gracile 0.11.0 = latest, next tags are 0.11.1-next.*) and gracile.js.org/docs (alpha-state caution, documented Express adapter, CSR add-on flagged experimental)
